The report checks fixed-R compact-eta Schwartz majorants, continuous finite density, real-mask/even-mu symmetry, Tonelli ball formula with the precise shift y+u and c_d^2 L^2 C_Gamma, and temperedness. The real/imaginary cross cancellation and absolute bilinear continuity extend the exact integral norm toL2 and bounded interval amplitudes. Both0<a<1 integrability and null-quotient semantics are preserved.

The delta kernel in step2 is interpreted as a distribution identity applied to the Schwartz product, not an ordinary convergent integral or infinite-measure oscillatory Fubini (R2). Finite covariance matrix order, independent Gaussian difference coupling and conditional Jensen forp>=1 are derived. No original-quotient multiplier or nonlinear solution comparison is inferred. The reviewer wording note about applying inversion again is at most presentational, not an actual missing normalization or derivation.

report_notes.classification: report-only absolute-phase equality overstatement; source bound is correct
report_notes.old: the absolute value of the right side equals the integral of the absolute Gaussian
report_notes.new: the absolute value of the right side is at most the integral of the absolute Gaussian
report_notes.contrary_calculation: Admissible d2,alpha1,Gamma=delta0(dx1)dx2, r1,y=(0,1): |integral exp(-|x|^2/4)exp(-iy.x)Gamma(dx)|=2sqrt(pi)exp(-1), whereas integral exp(-|x|^2/4)Gamma(dx)=2sqrt(pi).
report_notes.disposition: Raw report unchanged. The triangle inequality supplies precisely the correctly computed upper bound; the report reconstructs its scaling/prefactor/ball argument. A false equality is not adopted as a source fact. No manuscript change or critical missing public core is identified.

The delta formula is a tempered-distribution identity on the explicitly Schwartz product; it is not an ordinary scalar integral. Under this stated input its normalization is correct. The report uses a single Schwartz h in the spectral convention; no prohibited oscillatory Fubini is necessary. The reviewer note about inversion wording does not identify a source defect.

report_notes.classification: report-only unspecified ordinary versus unitary Fourier transform wording
report_notes.old: the Fourier transform of delta0(dx1)dx2 is(2pi)delta0(dxi2)
report_notes.new: its ordinary unnormalized transform is(2pi)delta0(dxi2); its d2 unitary transform is delta0(dxi2)
report_notes.disposition: The final spectral measure(2pi)^-1 dxi1 delta0(dxi2) is correct in Gamma=integral exp(i xi.x)mu. Direct pairing/inversion verifies it. No source correction or change of the counterexample is required.
